DAMGHANI:v1p396/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p396/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p396/r8.anchor: الرابع : الكبير العظيم قوله تعالى في سورة الرعد

ELMALILI:13:7-11/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r11.claim: God knows both the unseen and the witnessed, or the nonexistent and the existent.
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r11.anchor: O, gayba ve şehadete de âlim Allah, hislerden gāib olanı da bilir, hâzır olanı da. Veyahut ma‘dûmu da mevcûdu da bilir.

ELMALILI:13:7-11/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r12.claim: Because God knows the unseen and the witnessed, He knows whether sign-seekers want guidance or are acting from obstinacy.
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r12.anchor: âyet isteyenlerin hidâyet için mi, inad için mi ne gibi bir maksadla istediklerini de bilir.

ELMALILI:13:7-11/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r13.claim: Kabir means supremely great, with everything beneath God and nothing capable of encompassing Him; Muta‘ali means exalted in power and transcendent above created limits.
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r13.anchor: Kebîr yani her şey kendisinin dûnunda olan ve hiçbir vechile kābil-i ihâta olmayan yegâne büyük

ELMALILI:13:7-11/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r14.claim: Guidance belongs to God, and nothing lies outside His knowledge, power, or presence.
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r14.anchor: Onun için hidâyet O’na aittir. Ve O’nun ilm ü kudretinden hâriç kalacak ve huzûr u likāsına çıkmayacak hiçbir şey yoktur.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi rejects the codices' Madinan classification: in his view, the sūra is wholly Makkan, with no Madinan verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Some codices regard it to be Madī nan, which I fail to understand. Not one of its verse is Mad īnan in my opinion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: People should not compare God's knowledge with their own limits: he knows the unknown and manifest, and others know his plans only as much as he reveals.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: His knowledge embraces the known and the unknown. Only He knows His own intentions and schemes and others know about them to the extent He wants to reveal to them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p356/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p356/r10.speaker: أبو يعقوب الأزرق عن ورش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p356/r10.claim: Al-Azraq reports that Warsh may choose either to retain or omit yāʾ at pauses throughout this category of indefinite, declinable words.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p356/r10.anchor: وفيه عن أبي يعقوب الأزرق عن ورش أنه خيره في الوقف في جميع الباب، بين أن يقف بالياء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r9.claim: After citing hidden particulars, the passage states that God's knowledge encompasses all things, including what people witness and what escapes their senses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r9.anchor: ولما ذكر أنه عالم بأشياء خفية لا يعلمها إلا هو، وكانت أشياء جزئية من خفايا علمه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r10.claim: The unseen and witnessed may mean absent and existent, or what is absent from the senses and what is present to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r10.anchor: وقيل: الغائب المعدوم، والشاهد الموجود. وقيل: الغائب ما غاب عن الحس، والشاهد ما حضر للحس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r11.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r11.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads عالم الغيب with the accusative ending.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r11.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: عالم الغيب بالنصب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r12.claim: الكبير means majestic in rank, with all things beneath Him; المتعال means exalted above everything by power, or transcendent above the qualities of originated beings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r12.anchor: الكبير العظيم الشأن الذي كل شيء دونه، المتعال المستعلي على كل شيء بقدرته،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r13.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r13.claim: Ibn Kathir and, in one transmission, Abu Amr retain the yāʾ in المتعال both in pause and continuation; the other readers omit it, matching the written form, while Sibawayh cites omission in verse endings and rhymes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r13.anchor: وأثبت ابن كثير وأبو عمرو في رواية: ياء المتعال وقفا ووصلا، وهو الكثير في لسان العرب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r1.claim: God knows the unseen and the witnessed and is exalted above everything through His power.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r1.anchor: {عالم الغيب والشهادة الكبير} الذي كل شيء دونه، {المتعال} المستعلي على كل شيء بقدرته.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.claim: Al-Raʿd’s aim is to portray revelation as true in itself: sometimes its sound and fame move people toward guidance, while sometimes it instead leaves them blind and astray, like thunder whose lightning and rain may benefit, fail, or harm according to where they fall.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.anchor: مقصودها وصف الكتاب بأنه الحق في نفسه ، وتارة يتأثر عنه مع أن له صوتا وصيتا وإرعابا وإرهابا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r1.claim: Al-shahādah is a verbal noun used with passive meaning for things witnessed: visible objects and other perceptible things, thus joining the unseen and witnessed into all existence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r1.anchor: فهي هنا مصدر بمعنى المفعول ، أي الأشياء المشهودة ، وهي الظاهرة المحسوسة ، المرئيات وغيرها من المحسوسات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r2.claim: Al-kabīr metaphorically denotes greatness; language of size and multitude became conventional for majesty through comparing abstract meaning to sensory magnitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r2.anchor: والكبير : مجاز في العظمة ، إذ قد شاع استعمال أسماء الكثرة وألفاظ الكبر في العظمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r3.claim: Al-mutaʿāl means exalted; its tafaʿul form marks elevation as an inherent attribute, necessary in itself rather than conferred by another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r3.anchor: والمتعالي : المترفع . وصيغت الصفة بصيغة التفاعل للدلالة على أن العلو صفة ذاتية له لا من غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r4.claim: The exaltation means either complete invincibility, beyond any being's power to overcome or compel, or transcendence above deficiencies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r4.anchor: والمراد بالرفعة هنا المجاز عن العزة التامة بحيث لا يستطيع موجود أن يغلبه أو يكرهه ، أو المنزه عن النقائص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r5.claim: The final yāʾ in al-mutaʿāl is omitted to fit the verse endings, including the cadence shared with wāl and al-āṣāl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r5.anchor: وحذف الياء من المتعال } لمرعاة الفواصل الساكنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r6.claim: Sībawayh says yāʾs and wāws normally preferred in form may be dropped in verse endings and rhyme; retaining them is more analogical, while deletion is common Arabic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p98/r6.anchor: وقد ذكر سيبويه أن ما يختار إثباته من الياءات والواوات يحذف في الفواصل والقوافي ، والإثبات أقيس والحذف عربي كثير

TABATABAI:13:7-16#4/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#4/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:13:7-16#4/r11.claim: A report from Tha'laba ibn Maymun defines the unseen as what has not been and the witnessed as what has already been.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#4/r11.anchor: قال الغيب ما لم يكن والشهادة ما قد كان

TABATABAI:13:7-16#4/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#4/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16#4/r12.claim: Al-Tabatabai clarifies that “what has not been” means a potential reality not yet actualized, rather than sheer nonexistence; the report gives one instance of the concept.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#4/r12.anchor: ليس المراد من { ما لم يكن } المعدوم الذي ليس بشيء بل الأمر الذي بالقوة ما لم يدخل في ظرف الفعلية

TABRISI:13:8-11/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-11/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-11/r11.claim: “Al-mutaʿālī” and “al-ʿālī” mean the same; alternatively, “the Exalted” is omnipotent in a way no equal can share.
TABRISI:13:8-11/r11.anchor: المتعالي والعالي واحد وتعالى أي جل عن كل ثناء وقيل المتعالي المقتدر على وجه يستحيل أن يساويه غيره

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:9-11/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:9-11/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:9-11/r1.claim: God knows what is hidden from all creation and what creation witnesses; He is great in rank and exalted above the polytheists' claims.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:9-11/r1.anchor: ما غاب عن جميع خلقه { والشهادة } وما شهده الخلق { الكبير } العظيم القدر

SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r1.claim: عالم الغيب can be subject with الكبير المتعال as predicate, or predicate of an omitted subject هو.
SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { عالم الغيب }: يجوز أن يكون مبتدأ وخبره { الكبير المتعال } ، وأن يكون خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads عالم in the accusative as praise.
SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي " عالم " نصبا على المدح.

SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir and one Abu Amr narration retain the final yāʾ of المتعال in pause and continuation; others drop it in both, following the rasm. Sibawayh permits deletion at verse endings and because أل replaces tanwin.
SAMIN-DURR:13:9/r3.anchor: ووقف ابن كثير وأبو عمرو في رواية على ياء " المتعال " وصلا ووقفا

ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n20/r1.claim: Asad refers readers to his note 65 on surah 6 for related explanation.

ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r1.claim: Al-muta'al occurs only once in the Qur'an, here.
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r1.anchor: which occurs in the Qur'an only in this one instance

ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r2.claim: The attribute denotes God's infinite exaltedness above everything existing or possible.
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r2.anchor: denotes His infinite exaltedness above anything existing or potential

ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r3.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r3.claim: Zamakhshari adds that God is above anything that human definitions can circumscribe.
ASAD-NOTES:13:9#n21/r3.anchor: according to Zamakhshari, above anything that could be circumscribed by human definitions

IBNMUJAHID:v1p357/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p357/r2.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو عن عبد الوارث، أبو عمرو عن أبي زيد
IBNMUJAHID:v1p357/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr and two transmissions from Abū ʿAmr retain yāʾ in المتعال in connection and pause; others omit it in both.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p357/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ﴿ المتعال سواء منكم ﴾ بياء فى الوصل والوقف وكذلك قال الحلوانى عن أبى معمر المنقرى عن عبد الوارث عن أبى عمرو

NASHR:v2p192/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p192/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v2p192/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir affirms the extra yāʾ in المتعال both in connection and at pause through both transmissions; reports from Qunbul delete it in both or only at pause, but the author adopts affirmation.
NASHR:v2p192/r2.anchor: وأما المتعال، وهو في الرعد فوافقه على الإثبات في الحالين ابن كثير من روايتيه من غير خلاف

QIRAAT-ER:13:9:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:13:9:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:13:9:6#1/r1.claim: The variant retains the full final yāʾ in pause and connection, making the active participle morphologically complete without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:13:9:6#1/r1.anchor: Full yāʾ retained in pause and connection — canonical variant; makes the active participle morphologically complete

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r1.claim: Al-ghayb is what the senses cannot perceive and al-shahāda what they can; the paired terms intensify the sense of encompassing knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r1.anchor: أي الغائب عن الحس ( والشهادة ( أي الحاضر له عبر عنهما بهما مبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in a report from Ibn Abī Ḥātim, glosses the unseen as secret and the witnessed as public.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r2.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس أن الغيب السر والشهادة العلانية

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r3.claim: Another explanation takes al-ghayb as the nonexistent and al-shahāda as the existent.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī condemns the claim that God does not know the unseen because nothing is unseen to Him and nonexistent things are witnessed, calling it audacious and contrary to this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r4.anchor: أنه سبحانه لايعلم الغيب على معنى ان لاغيب بالنسبة اليه جل شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r5.claim: ʿĀlim is nominative either as the predicate of an omitted subject or as a second predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r5.anchor: ورفع ( عالم ) على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو خبر بعد خبر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r6.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r6.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads ʿālim in the accusative as an expression of praise.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r6.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( عالم ) بالنصب على المدح

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r7.claim: The description supplies evidence for the preceding assertion that God knows all things.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r7.anchor: وهذا الكلام كالدليل على ماقبله من قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r8.claim: Al-kabīr means immense in rank, with everything else beneath Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r8.anchor: العظيم الشأن الذي كل شيء دونه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r9.claim: Al-mutaʿāl means exalted above everything in His essence, knowledge, and all attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r9.anchor: المستعلي على كل شيء في ذاته وعلمه وسائر صفاته سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r10.claim: An alternative construes both names as declaring God above the creaturely attributes ascribed to Him by disbelievers, as in 37:159.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r10.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المعنى الكبير الذي يجل عما نعته به الخلق من صفات المخلوقين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r11.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r11.claim: Al-Ṭībī says these names, read with “Knower of unseen and witnessed,” add greatness and power to knowledge, against Christian and polytheist claims.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r11.anchor: قال العلامة الطيبي : إن معنى ( الكبير المتعال ) بالنسبة إلى مردوفه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r12.claim: Al-kabīr may be a second predicate; another parse makes ʿālim the subject and al-kabīr its predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110/r12.anchor: ورفع ( الكبير ) على أنه خبر بعد خبر وجوز أن يكون ( عالم ) مبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r1.claim: Taʾwīl derives from return; deriving it instead from siyāsa, management, as if the interpreter directs speech and places its meaning, is unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r1.anchor: والتأويل من الأول وهو الرجوع والقول بأنه من الأيالة وهي السياسة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda treats tafsir and taʾwīl as synonymous.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r3.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r3.claim: Al-Raghib says tafsir is broader and more often concerns words and individual expressions in divine books and others, while taʾwīl concerns meanings and whole constructions in divine books specifically.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r3.anchor: الراغب : التفسير أعم وأكثر إستعماله في الألفاظ ومفرداتها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r4.speaker: الماتريدي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r4.claim: Al-Maturidi distinguishes decisive assertion of God's intended meaning as tafsir from preferring one possible meaning without certainty as taʾwīl.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r4.anchor: الماتريدي : التفسير القطع بأن مراد الله تعالى كذا والتأويل ترجيح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r5.claim: Another distinction says tafsir depends on transmitted reports whereas taʾwīl depends on reasoned analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r5.anchor: وقيل التفسير ما يتعلق بالرواية والتأويل ما يتعلق بالدراية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r6.claim: If the distinction is conventional, earlier definitions do not match current usage: taʾwīl now commonly means sacred allusions and divine insights unveiled to spiritual wayfarers, while tafsir means something else; if based on literal implication, the distinctions should be reconsidered, though every unveiling entails a return and every return an unveiling.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r6.anchor: إذ قد تعارف من غير نكير أن التأويل إشارة قدسية ومعارف سبحانية تنكشف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r7.claim: Qur'anic interpretation is needed because understanding its legal rulings, the basis of lasting happiness and the straight path, is difficult and requires God's enabling grace.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r7.anchor: فلأن فهم القرآن العظيم المشتمل على الأحكام الشرعية التي هي مدار السعادة الأبدية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r8.claim: Even eloquent Companions with hearts illuminated by prophecy repeatedly asked the Prophet about matters they had not understood, and sometimes misunderstood God's intent, as Adi ibn Hatim did with the white and black thread; people today need interpretation at least as much.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p4#2/r8.anchor: كما وقع لعدي بن حاتم في الخيط الأبيض والأسود ولا شك أنا محتاجون

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r1.claim: The unseen is what the senses cannot perceive.

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r2.claim: The manifest is what is present to the senses.

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r3.claim: The Great is so majestic that nothing falls outside His knowledge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r3.anchor: { الكبير } العظيم الشأن الذي لا يخرج عن علمه شيء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r4.claim: The Exalted is supreme over all by power, or too exalted to bear created attributes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:9/r4.anchor: { المتعال } المستعلي على كل شيء بقدرته، أو الذي كبر عن نعت المخلوقين وتعالى عنه.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r4.claim: Since the requesters are obstinate rather than seeking guidance, God does not grant their proposed signs; instead He points to familiar acts proving His knowledge and power and the possibility of resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r4.anchor: يقرر من أفعاله المحسوسة لهم المقتضية لاتصافه من العلم والقدرة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r5.claim: If resurrection seems impossible, it is like the first creation; distinguishing a creature's dust after it scatters is less astonishing than distinguishing reproductive fluid from other mixed water.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r5.anchor: تمييز التراب الذي كان منه الحيوان

BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r15.speaker: الرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r15.claim: Al-Rummānī defines the unseen as what is hidden from every creature and the manifest as what appears to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r15.anchor: قال الرماني : الغيب : كون الشيء بحيث يخفى عن الحس , والشهادة : كونه بحيث يظهر له

BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r16.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r16.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines greatness as an evident disparity of degree: only God has absolute greatness, while human claims to grandeur diminish people and end in public humiliation at resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r16.anchor: قال الإمام أبو الحسن الحرالي : والكبر : ظهور التفاوت في ظاهر وباهر القدر الذي لا يحتاج إلى فكر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r17.claim: God is beyond approach in essence, attribute, or action; the reciprocal form intensifies the sense of transcendence.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r17.anchor: من أوج علوه في ذات أو صفة أو فعل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r18.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r18.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says transcendence means lying beyond reach by judgment or proof: imagined arguments are refuted by God's decisive proof, and He is exalted in knowledge, judgment, and argument.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r18.anchor: وقال أبوالحسن الحرالي رحمه الله : والتعالي

BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r19.claim: The preceding descriptions are as much as human reason can bear; the truth of God's attributes is absolute greatness and transcendence.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p128/r19.anchor: أشار إلى أن ذلك على ما تحتمله العقول

BURSEVI:v4p228/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p228/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p228/r1.claim: ʿĀlim al-ghayb is the predicate of an omitted subject; the definite article is comprehensive, covering all that can be called unseen.
BURSEVI:v4p228/r1.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف واللام للاستغراق أي هو تعالى عالم كل ما يطلق عليه اسم الغيب

BURSEVI:v4p228/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p228/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p228/r2.claim: The unseen includes what is hidden from perception, concealed knowledge and secrets, and the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v4p228/r2.anchor: وهو ما غاب عن الحس فيدخل فيه المعلومات والأسرار الخفية والآخرة

BURSEVI:v4p228/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p228/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v4p228/r3.claim: Some say Quranic attribution of unseen knowledge to God is relative to humans, since nothing is unseen to God.
BURSEVI:v4p228/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : ما ورد في القرآن من إسناد علم الغيب إلى الله تعالى إنما هو بالنسبة إلينا إذ لا غيب بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v4p228/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p228/r4.speaker: بعض سادات الصوفية
BURSEVI:v4p228/r4.claim: Some Sufi masters say that pure essence, beyond all relations, has no scientific relation and thus no knowledge of unseen in that respect; knowledge remains at the level of attributes and determinations.
BURSEVI:v4p228/r4.anchor: وقال بعض سادات الصوفية قدس الله أسرارهم : لما سقطت جميع النسب والإضافات في مرتبة الذات البحت والهوية الصرفة انتفت النسبة العلمية

BURSEVI:v4p228/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p228/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p228/r5.claim: Al-shahāda includes everything present to the senses, including perceptible beings, public things, and the world.
BURSEVI:v4p228/r5.anchor: والشهادة أي : كل ما يطلق عليه اسم الشهادة وهو ما حضر للحس فيدخل فيه الموجودات المدركة والعلانية والدنيا

BURSEVI:v4p228/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p228/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p228/r6.claim: Al-Kabīr is majestic in status, with nothing outside His knowledge; al-Mutaʿāl is exalted over all things by His power.
BURSEVI:v4p228/r6.anchor: الكبير العظيم الشأن الذي لا يخرج عن علمه شيء المتعال المستعلي على كل شيء بقدرته

BURSEVI:v4p228/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p228/r7.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v4p228/r7.claim: Al-Kawāshī explains God's transcendence as being above creaturely attributes and the claims of polytheists.
BURSEVI:v4p228/r7.anchor: وفي الكواشي : عن صفات المخلوقين وقول المشركين

DURR-FULL:v4p610/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the unseen and witnessed as secret and public.
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله {عالم الغيب والشهادة} قال: السر والعلانية

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the unseen and the witnessed as the secret and the public.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : عالم الغيب والشهادة قال : السر والعلانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p97/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p97/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p97/r9.claim: ‘Knower of the unseen and the visible’ sums up the universal reach of knowledge over hidden and manifest things, the two classes of existent things; the unseen was mentioned at the start of al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p97/r9.anchor: وجملة { عالم الغيب والشهادة } تذييل وفذلكة لتعميم العلم بالخفيات والظواهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r2.claim: The unseen is what perception cannot reach and the witnessed is what is observed; abstract nouns stand for things characterized by either condition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r2.anchor: والغيب: ما غاب عن الإدراكات، والشهادة: ما شوهد من الأمور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r3.claim: “Everything with Him is measured” is a general statement about everything subject to determination.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r3.anchor: وكل شيء عنده بمقدار لفظ عام في كل ما يدخله التقدير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r4.claim: Al-kabīr is an unrestricted attribute of majesty.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr and, in some reports, Abū ʿAmr retain the yāʾ in both connected reading and pause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r6.anchor: فأثبت ابن كثير وأبو عمرو- في بعض ما روي عنه- الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r7.speaker: الباقون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r7.claim: The remaining readers omit the yāʾ both when connecting and pausing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r7.anchor: ولم يثبتها الباقون في وصل ولا وقف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers retaining the yāʾ as the regular form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r8.anchor: ولم يثبتها الباقون في وصل ولا وقف. وإثباتها هو الوجه والباب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r9.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r9.claim: Sībawayh permits deleting yāʾ in verse-end pauses by analogy with poetic rhyme, but regards deletion elsewhere as poor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r9.anchor: واستسهل سيبويه حذفها في الفواصل- كهذه الآية- قياسا على القوافي في الشعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r18.claim: Sībawayh permits deleting yāʾ with tanwīn because tanwīn alternates with the definite article, and yāʾ is deleted with tanwīn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p298/r18.anchor: ولكن وجهه أنه لما كان التنوين يعاقب الألف واللام أبدا، وكانت هذه الياء تحذف مع التنوين، حسن أن تحذف مع معاقبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r1.claim: The explanation of ‘Knower of the unseen and the manifest’ was given earlier in the discussion of al-Anʿām.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ( عالم الغيب والشهادة ) قد شرحنا ذلك في ( الأنعام 6 )

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r2.claim: Al-Kabīr means supremely great in rank and deserving of exalted attributes; every other greatness is small beside God, who is also beyond resemblance to creatures.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r2.anchor: و ( الكبير ) بمعنى العظيم ومعناه يعود إلى كبر قدره واستحقاقه صفات العلو فهو أكبر من كل كبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir reads المتعالي with final yāʾ both in connected recitation and at pause; al-Warith reports the same from Abu Amr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r3.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير المتعالي بياء في الوصل والوقف وكذلك روى عبد الوارث عن أبي عمرو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r4.speaker: ابن شنبوذ عن قنبل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r4.claim: Ibn Shanabudh's report from Qunbul retains the yāʾ at pause but omits it in connected recitation; the other readers omit it in both.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r4.anchor: واثبتها في الوقف دون الوصل ابن شنبوذ عن قنبل والباقون بغير ياء في الحالين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r5.claim: Al-Mutaʿālī means the one transcendent above the attributes of created beings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r5.anchor: والمتعالي هو المتنزه عن صفات المخلوقين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r6.speaker: الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r6.claim: Al-Khattabi says al-Mutaʿālī may mean the one high above His creation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r6.anchor: قال الخطابي وقد يكون بمعنى العالي فوق خلقه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r7.claim: Al-Hasan explains al-Mutaʿālī as transcendent above what the polytheists say.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p308#3/r7.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أنه قال المتعالي عما يقول المشركون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p436/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p436/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p436/r3.claim: God knows everything witnessed and unseen, and nothing is hidden from Him; He is greater than everything, exalted over all, all-knowing and all-subduing, so all submit willingly or unwillingly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p436/r3.anchor: وقوله: {عالم الغيب والشهادة} أي: يعلم كل شيء مما يشاهده العباد ومما يغيب عنهم

JISHUMI:v5p3750/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r6.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir and Yaʿqub retain the final yāʾ in pause and continuation, following the original form.
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ويعقوب: المتعالي بإثبات الياء في الوقف والوصل على الأصل

JISHUMI:v5p3750/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r7.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r7.claim: The other readers delete the yāʾ in both positions for ease of pronunciation.
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r7.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بحذف الياء في الحالين للتخفيف

JISHUMI:v5p3750/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r13.claim: The unseen is hidden from the senses; the witnessed is what appears to them.
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r13.anchor: والغيب: ما غاب عن الحواس، غاب غيبا، وغيبه تغييبا

JISHUMI:v5p3750/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r14.claim: Al-mutaʿali and al-ʿali mean the same; God is exalted beyond every report, or is powerful beyond comparison.
JISHUMI:v5p3750/r14.anchor: والمتعالي والعالي واحد، ومنه: تعالى؛ أي: جل عن كل نبأ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p484#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p484#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p484#2/r6.claim: God's knowledge and measure show that differing signs are deliberate acts of wisdom; He would have granted their requested sign if doing so were beneficial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p484#2/r6.anchor: ولقد دل بما أردفه من ذكر آيات علمه وتقديره الأشياء على قضايا حكمته

MUQATIL:13:8-9/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:8-9/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:8-9/r5.claim: The unseen includes the fetus in the womb and everything unseen; the witnessed includes the fetus and all else visible.
MUQATIL:13:8-9/r5.anchor: يعني غيب الولد في بطن أمه

MUQATIL:13:8-9/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:8-9/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:8-9/r6.claim: God is the greatest, with none greater than Him, and is exalted above His creation.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r1.claim: The unseen is what is hidden from creation, and the visible is what they witness.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ عالم الغيب ﴾ ما غاب عن الخلق ﴿ والشهادة ﴾ ما شاهدوه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r2.claim: Al-Kabīr means immense in rank, with everything beneath Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r2.anchor: العظيم الشأن الذي كل شيء دونه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r3.claim: Al-Mutaʿāl means either above everything by His power or exalted beyond the attributes of creatures.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r3.anchor: المستعلى على كل شيء بقدرته أو الذي كبر عن صفات المخلوقين وتعالى عنها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#3/r4.claim: Makkī reads with yāʾ in both forms of the final pair of divine names.

QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r13.claim: Al-ghayb and al-shahadah are verbal nouns meaning what is absent and what is witnessed; God knows both what creation cannot see and what it sees.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r13.anchor: والشهادة مصدر بمعنى الشاهد فنبه سبحانه على انفراده بعلم الغيب

QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r14.claim: The verse praises God’s exclusive knowledge of the unseen and hidden; no one may share in that knowledge with Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r14.anchor: لا يجوز أن يشاركه في ذلك أحد

QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r15.claim: Physicians may infer from indications and signs, but claiming certainty from them is unbelief; treating them as experience is acceptable because custom can fail while knowledge cannot change.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r15.anchor: وإن قالوا إنها تجربة تركوا وما هم عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r16.claim: Al-Kabir means that everything is beneath Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r16.anchor: و { الكبير } الذي كل شيء دونه

QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r17.claim: Al-Mutaʿali is exalted above the polytheists’ claims and prevails over everything through power and domination.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:8-9#3/r17.anchor: عما يقول المشركون، المستعلي على كل شيء بقدرته وقهره

QASHANI:13:8-9/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:8-9/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:8-9/r5.claim: God knows both the unseen receptivity in people’s capacities and the manifest perfections already brought into actuality.
QASHANI:13:8-9/r5.anchor: غيب ما في الاستعدادات من قوة القبول وشهادة الكمالات الحاضرة الخارجة إلى الفعل

QASHANI:13:8-9/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:8-9/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:8-9/r6.claim: His greatness means that He does not fail to give what any capacity requires, for He encompasses all capacities and grants each its due.
QASHANI:13:8-9/r6.anchor: الشأن الذي يجل عن إعطاء ما يقتضيه بعض الاستعدادات بل يسع كلها فيعطيها مقتضياتها

QASHANI:13:8-9/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:8-9/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:8-9/r7.claim: His exaltedness means His effusion never ceases, so He does not delay once readiness occurs or give less than it requires.
QASHANI:13:8-9/r7.anchor: عن أن ينقطع فيضه فيتأخر عن حصول الاستعداد وينقص مما يقتضيه

RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as God's knowledge of what is hidden from creation and what they witness.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يريد علم ما غاب عن خلقه وما شهدوه

RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r6.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi says that on Ibn Abbas's explanation, ghayb is an absent or hidden thing and shahāda is a present or witnessed thing.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r6.anchor: قال الواحدي : فعلى هذا ( الغيب ) مصدر يريد به الغائب

RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r7.claim: One reported interpretation defines the hidden as what is known and the manifest as what exists.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم : الغائب هو المعلوم ، والشاهد هو الموجود

RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r8.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r8.claim: Another interpretation distinguishes what is beyond the senses from what is present to the senses.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون : الغائب ما غاب عن الحس ، والشاهد ما حضر

RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r9.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r9.claim: A third interpretation calls what creatures do not know hidden and what they know manifest.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون : الغائب ما لا يعرفه الخلق ، والشاهد ما يعرفه الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r10.claim: Razi classifies known things as existent or nonexistent, each either necessarily so or possibly otherwise, and says God knows every category and its properties.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r10.anchor: ونقول : المعلومات قسمان : المعلومات والموجودات ، والمعدومات منها معدومات يمتنع وجودها

RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r11.speaker: إمام الحرمين
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r11.claim: Imam al-Haramayn says God's known objects are infinite and each has infinitely many possible states; God knows in detail every possible location and quality of an indivisible atom.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14/r11.anchor: عن إمام الحرمين رحمهم الله تعالى أنه كان يقول لله تعالى معلومات لا نهاية لها

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r1.claim: God cannot be 'great' in body, volume, or size; the word therefore denotes greatness in power and divine measures.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r1.anchor: وهو تعالى يمتنع أن يكون كبيرا بحسب الجثة والحجم والمقدار ، فوجب أن يكون كبيرا بحسب القدرة

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r2.claim: Al-Mutaʿāl means God is exalted above anything impermissible, in His essence, attributes, and acts.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r2.anchor: ثم وصف تعالى نفسه بأنه المتعال وهو المتنزه عن كل ما لا يجوز عليه

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.claim: God's complete knowledge, power, and transcendence establish His ability to resurrect, give the signs disbelievers demand, and punish them; He delays these by will according to one group and by wisdom according to another.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.anchor: فهذه الآية دالة على كونه تعالى موصوفا بالعلم الكامل والقدرة التامة ، ومنزها عن كل ما لا ينبغي

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir retains the yāʾ in al-mutaʿālī in both connected and paused recitation; the other readers drop it in both for ease.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ( المتعالي ) بإثبات الياء في الوقف والوصل على الأصل

STUDYQURAN:13:8/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:8/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:8/r4.claim: God as Knower of the Unseen and the seen is also described in 6:59 and 59:22.
STUDYQURAN:13:8/r4.anchor: For God as Knower of the Unseen and the seen, see 6:59; 59:22c.

SULAMI:v1p328#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p328#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p328#2/r1.claim: The true knower perceives visible and hidden things equally without inference; ultimately, true knowledge belongs to God, great in essence and exalted in attributes.
SULAMI:v1p328#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : العالم على الحقيقة ، من يكون الشاهد والغائب عنده سواء في العلم لا بأن يستدل

SULAMI:v1p328#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p328#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p328#2/r2.claim: God knows what is concealed within a person before it appears and knows the intentions behind deeds as they become manifest.
SULAMI:v1p328#2/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : عالم بما غيب فيك مما لا تعلمه من نفسك قبل أن يبديها أو يظهرها وعالم بما يبدو من أفعالك

SULAMI:v1p328#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p328#2/r3.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p328#2/r3.claim: God's greatness fills the hearts of gnostics, making all else small; His exaltedness means approach depends on the dispensation of His generosity.
SULAMI:v1p328#2/r3.anchor: قال جعفر : في قوله : الكبير المتعال : كبير في قلوب العارفين محله فصغر عندهم كل ما سواه

TAB-FULL:v13p452#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p452#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p452#2/r1.claim: The Most High is exalted above everything by His power.
TAB-FULL:v13p452#2/r1.anchor: بقدرته، وهو المتفاعل من العلو مثل المتقارب من القرب،

TAB-FULL:v13p452#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p452#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p452#2/r2.claim: Al-mutaʿāl is the derived form mutafāʿil, from ʿuluww, like al-mutaqārib from qurb and al-mutadānī from dunūw.
TAB-FULL:v13p452#2/r2.anchor: وهو المتفاعل من العلو مثل المتقارب من القرب، والمتداني من الدنو

TABATABAI:13:9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:9/r1.claim: Unseen and manifest are relational: one thing may be hidden from one being yet evident to another, depending on what lies within each being's limits.
TABATABAI:13:9/r1.anchor: الغيب والشهادة كما سمعت مرارا معنيان إضافيان فالشيء الواحد يمكن أن يكون غيبا بالنسبة إلى شيء وشهادة بالنسبة إلى آخر

TABATABAI:13:9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:9/r2.claim: Only God knows the unseen: finite beings cannot encompass what exceeds their existential limits, whereas God's unbounded existence encompasses everything, making both unseen and manifest witnessed to Him.
TABATABAI:13:9/r2.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن الغيب لا يعلم به إلا الله سبحانه أما أنه لا يصير معلوما لشيء فلأن العلم نوع إحاطة

TABATABAI:13:9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:9/r3.claim: “Great” first describes comparative bodily size and later extends beyond bodies; for God it means possessing and encompassing every perfection, with more besides.
TABATABAI:13:9/r3.anchor: والذي يناسب ساحة قدسه تعالى من معنى الكبرياء أنه تعالى يملك كل كمال لشيء ويحيط به فهو تعالى كبير

TABATABAI:13:9#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:9#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:9#2/r1.claim: In 17:43, “greatly exalted” is an absolute object of “He is exalted,” expressing the intensive sense of “exaltation.”
TABATABAI:13:9#2/r1.anchor: قوله { علوا كبيرا } مفعول مطلق لقوله { تعالى } وموضوع في محل قولنا تعاليا

TABATABAI:13:9#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:9#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:9#2/r2.claim: God is ʿAlī because He is above and rules all things; He is mutaʿāl because His height is ultimate, surpassing every other height and dominating from every direction.
TABATABAI:13:9#2/r2.anchor: فهو سبحانه علي ومتعال أما أنه علي فلأنه علا كل شيء وتسلط عليه والعلو هو التسلط، وأما أنه متعال فلأن له

TABATABAI:13:9#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:9#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:9#2/r3.claim: Pairing the knowledge of unseen and manifest with God's greatness and exaltation signals that He encompasses and dominates everything, and nothing can overpower or escape His knowledge.
TABATABAI:13:9#2/r3.anchor: تظهر النكتة في تعقيب قوله { عالم الغيب والشهادة } بقوله { الكبير المتعال } لأن مفاد مجموع الاسمين أنه سبحانه محيط بكل شيء متسلط عليه

TABRISI:13:8-10/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-10/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-10/r9.claim: The phrase can mean knowledge of what is beyond people’s senses and what they witness, or of the nonexistent and existent; al-Ḥasan also glosses it as secret and public.
TABRISI:13:8-10/r9.anchor: أي عالم بما غاب عن حس العباد وبما يشاهده العباد

TABRISI:13:8-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-10/r10.claim: The author prefers a general sense covering every object of knowledge, existent or nonexistent.

TABRISI:13:8-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-10/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-10/r11.claim: Al-Kabīr may mean the master, king, and one able to do all things; alternatively, everything is beneath Him due to perfect attributes, or He is beyond resemblance to creatures.
TABRISI:13:8-10/r11.anchor: وهو السيد الملك القادر على جميع الأشياء

TABRISI:13:8-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-10/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-10/r12.claim: Al-Mutaʿālī is exalted over all by power and has no equal; He is transcendent above what is impermissible in His essence or acts and what polytheists claim.
TABRISI:13:8-10/r12.anchor: وهو الذي علا كل شيء بقدرته

THALABI:v5p273/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p273/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p273/r6.claim: God knows the unseen and the witnessed; al-Kabīr means everything is beneath Him, and al-Mutaʿāl means He is exalted over all by His power.
THALABI:v5p273/r6.anchor: عالم الغيب والشهادة الكبير الذي كل شيء دونه المتعال المستعلي على كل شيء بقدرته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God knows what is hidden from all creation and what creatures know; ghayb and shahadah mean the absent and the witnessed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬4): يريد علم ما غاب عن جميع خلقه، وما شهد بما علموا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r2.claim: Ghayb and shahadah are verbal nouns used for the absent and the witnessed; much of what is witnessed is known to creatures.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r2.anchor: فعلى هذا الغيب مصدر يريد به الغائب، ومثله الشهادة يريد به الشاهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r3.claim: Al-Kabir means great and majestic: God's rank and entitlement to exalted attributes make every other great thing small beside Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {الكبير} هو بمعنى العظيم والجليل، ومعناه يعود إلى كبر قدره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r4.claim: Al-Hasan glosses al-Mutaʿali as exalted above what the polytheists say.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r4.anchor: قال الحسن (¬5): المتعالي عما يقول المشركون.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r5.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r5.claim: Al-Azhari explains al-Mutaʿali as the One exalted above the heretics' impiety.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r5.anchor: قال الأزهري (¬1): المتعالي: الذي جل عن إلحاد الملحدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir retains the yāʾ of al-Mutaʿali both in connected recitation and at pause, which al-Wahidi calls the regular form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r6.anchor: وأثبت (¬2) ابن كثير (ياء)، المتعالي وقفا ووصلا، وهو القياس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r7.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r7.claim: Sibawayh says retaining yāʾ at pause is clearer when the definite article is present, since it remains in connected speech; indefinite forms such as qadin lose it in liaison.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r7.anchor: قال سيبويه (¬3): إذا لم يكن في موضع تنوين، فإن البيان أجود في الوقف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r8.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r8.claim: Some Arabs delete yāʾ at pause by analogy with indefinite forms; deleting it in connected speech is unexpected, but verse endings can imitate rhyme.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p302/r8.anchor: فأما من حذف في الوصل والوقف، فإن سيبويه زعم أن من العرب من يحذف هذا في الوقف

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r1.claim: Human knowledge is limited, incomplete, and changeable, while God's knowledge is infinite, complete, and certain, including every stage from conception to death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r1.anchor: İnsanların bilgisi sınırlı, eksik ve değişmeye açıktır. Allah’ın ilmi ise sonsuz, tam ve kesindir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r4.claim: The commentary directs readers to 2:3 for its discussion of the unseen and the seen.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r4.anchor: gayb ve şehâdet hakkında bilgi için bk. Bakara 2/3

BURHAN:v3p405/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p405/r2.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
BURHAN:v3p405/r2.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam asks why the more praiseworthy unseen is named before the witnessed, contrary to the usual rhetorical delay of the more praiseworthy.
BURHAN:v3p405/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عبد السلام في قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v3p405/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p405/r3.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
BURHAN:v3p405/r3.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam answers that God has more witnessed objects of knowledge, so the witnessed deserves to be delayed.
BURHAN:v3p405/r3.anchor: وأجاب بأن المشاهدات له أكثر من الغائب عنا

BURHAN:v3p405/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p405/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p405/r4.claim: The author objects that God's unseen is innumerable; instead, the wording rises to the more praiseworthy to show the unseen and witnessed are equal in His knowledge.
BURHAN:v3p405/r4.anchor: وقول الشيخ إن المشاهدات له أكثر فيه نظر بل في غيبه ما لايحصى

BURHAN:v3p405/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p405/r7.speaker: الشاعر
BURHAN:v3p405/r7.claim: A cited poet illustrates the maxim that the more important matter is placed first, which appears to challenge delaying the more praiseworthy quality.
BURHAN:v3p405/r7.anchor: وقال الشاعر … أبي دهرنا إسعافنا في نفوسنا

BURHAN:v3p405/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p405/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p405/r8.claim: The importance-first rule applies to distinct objects or purposes; delaying praise concerns two qualities of one thing, where reversing them would be pointless.
BURHAN:v3p405/r8.anchor: المراد بقوله فقدم الأهم فالأهم فيما إذا كانا شيئين متغايرين

NAHHAS:v2p351/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p351/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p351/r17.claim: عالم may be an adjective, an independent clause with an omitted subject, or a new subject whose predicate follows; it may also be accusative for praise or genitive in apposition.
NAHHAS:v2p351/r17.anchor: نعت وإن شئت على إضمار مبتدأ وإن شئت بالابتداء وما بعده خبره ويجوز في الإعراب النصب على المدح والخفض على البدل

NAHHAS:v2p351/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p351/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p351/r18.claim: الكبير means the sovereign able to do all things, and المتعال means exalted above all things.
NAHHAS:v2p351/r18.anchor: ( الكبير ) الملك المقتدر على كل شيء و ( المتعال ) المستعلي على كل شيء

NAHHAS:v2p351/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p351/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p351/r19.claim: The final yāʾ is omitted because the word ends a verse.

ITQAN:v2p343/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p343/r17.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p343/r17.claim: Al-ghayb wa-l-shahāda means the secret and the public, or hidden and witnessed.

NASHR:v2p186/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p186/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p186/r5.claim: Al-Dani judges disputed reports on extra yāʾs, including المهتد, المتعال, فاعتزلون, and ترجمون, erroneous; Ibn al-Jazari relies on established practice and trusted reports from Qunbul and the imams.
NASHR:v2p186/r5.anchor: وقد نص الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني على أن ذلك في هذه الياءات غلط قطع بذلك وجزم به

NASHR:v2p186/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p186/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p186/r6.claim: The author relies on established practice and sound transmission from Qunbul and trusted imams where reports on these extra yāʾs conflict.
NASHR:v2p186/r6.anchor: والذي أعول عليه في ذلك هو ما عليه العمل وصح عن قنبل، ونص عليه الأئمة الموثوق بهم

NASHR:v2p297#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p297#2/r9.speaker: ابن كثير، ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p297#2/r9.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb retain the extra yāʾ in both continuation and pause; a report from Shanbūdh via Qunbul deletes it in both states.
NASHR:v2p297#2/r9.anchor: المتعال أثبتها في الحالين ابن كثير ويعقوب، وتقدم ما روي فيها عن شنبوذ عن قنبل من حذفها في الحالين
